# Generated by gen_p01.py - do not edit by hand.
source Python's built-in pow(base, exp, mod) and pow(a, -1, mod), cross-checked with math.gcd
seed 1
compare records
explain _lines=R1
requirement R1 One output line per input line, in order: `modexp <result>` or `modinv <result>`/`modinv none`
requirement R2 exp = 0 gives 1 mod m (even if base = 0), except mod = 1 always gives 0
requirement R3 exp = 1 gives base mod m
requirement R4 Exponents hundreds of bits long finish well under the time limit (square-and-multiply, not a loop of `exp` multiplications)
requirement R5 base >= mod is reduced mod m before exponentiating
requirement R6 modinv returns the inverse when gcd(a, mod) = 1
requirement R7 modinv returns `none` when gcd(a, mod) != 1, including a = 0 and a sharing a prime factor with mod
requirement R8 mod = 1: modexp is always 0, and by convention modinv mod 1 is also 0
requirement E2E A real curve prime (P-384's p) used for one modexp and one modinv
case 01-R1-mixed R1
title five lines, modexp and modinv interleaved
input
modexp 3 5 7
modinv 3 7
modexp 10 0 13
modinv 6 13
modexp 2 10 1000
expected
modexp 5
modinv 5
modexp 1
modinv 11
modexp 24
end
